nodes.summary: For a dimension $d$, a ball tree over the integer points $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (functions $\{0, \dots, d-1\} \to \mathbb{Z}$) is either empty, a leaf holding one point, or a node holding a center point $c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, a natural number $b$ (the squared-radius bound of the node's sphere) and two child ball trees.
nodes.title: Ball tree

nodes.summary: The ball tree built from a list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is defined by recursion on the list. The empty list gives the empty tree and a one-point list $[p]$ gives the leaf $p$. A list $L = [x_1, \dots, x_n]$ with $n \ge 2$ gives a node whose center is $x_1$, whose bound is the squared radius of $L$ around $x_1$ (the largest squared distance from $x_1$ to a point of $L$), whose left child is the tree built from…
nodes.title: Building a ball tree by halving

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the squared distance from $p$ to $q$ equals the squared distance from $q$ to $p$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of squared distance

nodes.summary: Let $c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $L$ be a list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. For every point $p$ of $L$, the squared distance from $c$ to $p$ is at most the squared radius of $L$ around $c$, the largest squared distance from $c$ to a point of $L$.
nodes.title: Points lie within the squared radius

nodes.summary: For all points $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, writing $\delta(x, y)$ for the squared distance from $x$ to $y$, we have $\delta(a, c) \le 2\,(\delta(a, b) + \delta(b, c))$.
nodes.title: Relaxed triangle inequality for squared distance

nodes.summary: For points $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the squared distance from $p$ to $q$ is the natural number $\sum_{i=0}^{d-1} (p_i - q_i)^2$, computed in $\mathbb{Z}$ and then converted to $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Squared Euclidean distance

nodes.summary: For every ball tree $t$, the list of points stored in $t$, read from left to right, has length equal to the size of $t$.
nodes.title: Number of points of a ball tree

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, let $q, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $r$ be a natural number. Then $p$ is returned by the similarity search with query $q$ and squared radius $r$ on the ball tree built from $L$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $L$ and the squared distance from $q$ to $p$ is at most $r$.
nodes.title: Search of a built ball tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a ball tree satisfying the bounding-sphere invariant. For all $q, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every natural number $r$, $p$ is returned by the similarity search of $t$ with query $q$ and squared radius $r$ if and only if $p$ is one of the points stored in $t$ and the squared distance from $q$ to $p$ is at most $r$.
nodes.title: Search of a valid ball tree

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, $p$ is one of the points stored in the ball tree built from $L$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $L$.
nodes.title: Points of a built ball tree

nodes.summary: For a center $c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and a list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the squared covering radius of $P$ about $c$ is the largest squared distance from $c$ to a point of $P$, or $0$ if $P$ is empty.
nodes.title: Squared covering radius

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a dimension and write $\delta(x, y)$ for the squared distance from $x$ to $y$ in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. For a ball tree $T$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, a squared radius $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $A$ of points, the accumulating search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ with accumulator $A$ is $A$ when $T$ is empty; when $T$ is a leaf holding $p$, it is $p$ followed by $A$ if…
nodes.title: Accumulating ball-tree search

nodes.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, every query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, the search of the ball tree built from $P$ for $q$ and $r$ is a permutation of the sublist of $P$ consisting of the points $p$ whose squared distance from $q$ is at most $r$, kept with their multiplicities.
nodes.title: Ball-tree search of a built tree, up to order

nodes.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, every query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $T$ be the ball tree built from $P$. The search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ equals the list of points of $T$, from left to right, filtered to the points $p$ whose squared distance from $q$ is at most $r$, in their order.
nodes.title: Ball-tree search of a built tree

nodes.summary: For every ball tree $T$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ satisfying the bounding-sphere invariant, every query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, the search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ equals the list of points of $T$, from left to right, filtered to the points $p$ whose squared distance from $q$ is at most $r$, in their order. Pruning against the bounding spheres loses no point.
nodes.title: Ball-tree search is exact

nodes.summary: The search of a ball tree $T$ for a query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and a squared radius $r \in \mathbb{N}$ is the accumulating search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ started with the empty accumulator.
nodes.title: Ball-tree similarity search

nodes.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the size of the ball tree built from $P$ equals the length of $P$, that is, the number of entries of $P$ counted with repetition.
nodes.title: Size of a built ball tree

nodes.summary: The size of a ball tree is the number of points held in its leaves: it is $0$ for the empty tree, $1$ for a leaf, and the sum of the sizes of the two children for a node; the center of a node is not counted.
nodes.title: Size of a ball tree

nodes.summary: For a ball tree $T$ and a list $A$ of points, the accumulating traversal returns $A$ when $T$ is empty, the point $p$ followed by $A$ when $T$ is a leaf holding $p$, and, when $T$ is a node with children $L$ and $R$, the accumulating traversal of $L$ whose accumulator is the accumulating traversal of $R$ with accumulator $A$.
nodes.title: Accumulating traversal of a ball tree

nodes.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the list of points of the ball tree built from $P$, from left to right, is a permutation of $P$.
nodes.title: A built ball tree stores a permutation of its input

nodes.summary: The point list of a ball tree is the list of the points held at its leaves, from left to right: the empty tree gives the empty list, a leaf holding $p$ gives the list $[p]$, and a node gives the point list of its left subtree followed by the point list of its right subtree. The centers stored at nodes are not included.
nodes.title: Point list of a ball tree

nodes.summary: For every list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the ball tree built from it by recursive halving satisfies the bounding-sphere invariant.
nodes.title: Ball trees built by halving are valid

nodes.summary: Validity of a ball tree is defined inductively: the empty tree and every leaf are valid, and a node with center $c$ and squared-radius bound $b$ is valid when both of its subtrees are valid and every point in the point list of either subtree lies within squared Euclidean distance $b$ of $c$.
nodes.title: Bounding-sphere invariant of a ball tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
